question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: Three keyless GETs under the well-known prefix: the RFC 9728 path-inserted URL the challenge names, the well-known root, and a path invented for this pass (7c31ab90, fixed in the published program so a re-runner sends the same string). Then the authorization-server metadata and openid-configuration.

decoded.three-documents: Path-inserted /oauth-protected-resource/mcp at 12:31:02.729Z: 200, 134 bytes, sha256 18b9e6169cc08b20e368fe567d98660db120b36138f2d88ec7fe3fa975f39660, resource https://mcp.squareup.com/mcp. Well-known root at 12:31:03.010Z: 200, 1098 bytes, sha256 efdf8dd43b5fe7fe3b8d5d936c396bba9133e205e033ca7a7e6cff04dea130c6, the same resource plus scopes_supported with 48 names. Invented path /oauth-protected-resource/7c31ab90 at 12:31:03.286Z: 200, 139 bytes, sha256 87334a0d5108ea25cb40cbc9a39025642720851a288a9317f8409fbdfec7ffe7, declaring resource https://mcp.squareup.com/7c31ab90.
decoded.the-control: The invented path neither 404s nor returns the catch-all document: it returns a document GENERATED from the requested string, declaring as a protected resource a path that does not exist and naming https://mcp.squareup.com as its authorization server. On this host a 200 from that prefix is not evidence that the path is a resource, and the document's own resource field is not evidence either.
decoded.three-behaviours-measured: At the same prefix this researcher has now measured three behaviours in two days: mcp.asana.com and mcp.wix.com answer 404 to an invented path (9 and 13 bytes), mcp.figma.com answers ONE catch-all document for every path including an invented one (270 bytes, one digest), and mcp.squareup.com answers a per-path document it generates. A sweep reading only status codes scores all three identically, and the control costs one request.
decoded.the-challenge-points-at-the-thinner-docu: The 134-byte path-inserted document carries only resource, authorization_servers and bearer_methods_supported. The 1098-byte root carries those three plus scopes_supported with 48 Square OAuth scope names including PAYMENTS_WRITE, PAYMENTS_WRITE_IN_PERSON, PAYMENTS_WRITE_SHARED_ONFILE, PAYMENTS_WRITE_ADDITIONAL_RECIPIENTS, DISPUTES_WRITE, GIFTCARDS_WRITE, PAYOUTS_READ and SETTLEMENTS_READ. A client that follows the challenge, as RFC 9728 directs, never reads the scope list; a client that guesses the root path does.
decoded.authorization-server: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server at 12:31:03.584Z: 200, 590 bytes, sha256 29daeaedccd0b8d517cf3e0bf97a36650905cb334a2a72a33db2d0084d3af209. issuer https://mcp.squareup.com, so the resource host is its own authorization server; registration_endpoint https://mcp.squareup.com/register; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none]; code_challenge_methods_supported [plain, S256]; grant_types_supported [authorization_code, refresh_token]; revocation_endpoint equal to the token endpoint; and client_id_metadata_document_supported present and explicitly FALSE, where most hosts in this registry's census simply omit the key. openid-configuration answers 404 at 13 bytes, so it is not an alias here.
decoded.not-a-security-claim: Nothing here is a security claim. plain beside S256, and none among the token endpoint auth methods, are what the document says a client may offer; what the token endpoint accepts cannot be measured without registering a client and requesting a token, which is a credential and a write, and neither was done.
decoded.not-measured: whether the registration endpoint registers a client, any token request, and whether the scope list the root document publishes is the set an MCP client can actually be granted.

finding: mcp.squareup.com serves a protected-resource document for ANY path under its well-known prefix and builds each one from the path requested: a path invented for this pass, 7c31ab90, answered 200 with 139 bytes declaring resource https://mcp.squareup.com/7c31ab90, a resource that does not exist. The two real documents also differ, and the challenge points at the thinner one: the path-inserted document is 134 bytes with three fields, while the well-known root is 1098 bytes and adds scopes_supported with 48 Square scope names including four PAYMENTS_WRITE variants. The authorization server is the resource host itself, advertising dynamic client registration, token auth none, plain beside S256, and client_id_metadata_document_supported explicitly false. Three behaviours of this prefix are now measured across five hosts, and only an invented path tells them apart.
